items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I used to make candy-spending money from Mrs. Copland by watering her lawn in the summer and shoveling coal into her cellar in the winter.

ctx.x: Some months later my father decided to go back to Cincinnati and that was very pleasing to me because the only boy around me on the farm with Aunt Amanda was her son Tom and I was happy at the thought of seeing Eddie Partridge, Eddie West, who lived on Hathaway Street and with whom I used to draw pictures of fine looking automobiles, and many of the other boys that were in my gang.

We lived on the 5th Street between Mound and Cutter Street over an undertaker parlor. The name of the undertaker was Mr. Copeland. When we lived on Barr Street, the Coplands lived across the street from me and I used to make candy-spending money from Mrs. Copland by watering her lawn in the summer and shoveling coal into her cellar in the winter.

Dolly Jones left Cincinnati along with her mother who's name was Dyer Jones. Some medicine shows came to town and they used to put on their show in any empty lot they could find and no one had to pay to see them. The supposed doctor sold bottles of syrup that was supposed to be good for the liver, rheumatism, heart trouble, and pills for blood circulation, aching bones or any kind of sickness that existed. Medicine to cure all ailments.
